This topic covers the response_format parameter, strict mode guaranteeing schema conformance, passing a Pydantic model directly through the SDK, the difference between best-effort JSON mode and strict schema mode, and documented limitations worth knowing about.
1. A Concrete Implementation of Schema Enforcement

blocks.title: Diagram summary
blocks.content: Building on streaming responses, structured outputs here means concrete schema enforcement

blocks.text: This connects directly to schema-based outputs, covered generally in an earlier module, OpenAI offers a concrete, specific implementation of that same general idea, constraining the model generation itself to match a provided JSON schema.
2. The response_format Parameter

blocks.title: Diagram summary
blocks.content: The response_format parameter accepts a provided JSON schema

blocks.text: Setting response_format on a request lets you pass a JSON schema definition directly, exactly the schema concept covered in the earlier Schema-Based Outputs topic, now expressed as this specific provider parameter.
3. Strict Mode Guarantees Schema Conformance

blocks.title: Diagram summary
blocks.content: Setting strict to true guarantees output matches the schema

blocks.text: Setting strict to true is what actually enforces the schema at the generation level, this connects directly to the reliability tiers covered in the earlier Schema-Based Outputs topic, strict mode is the strongest guarantee available, output is constrained during generation itself rather than merely hoped for through instruction wording.
4. Passing a Pydantic Model Directly

blocks.title: Diagram summary
blocks.content: A Pydantic model definition gets passed directly to the SDK, generating the schema automatically

blocks.text: This connects directly to Pydantic models, covered in an earlier module, the official OpenAI SDK lets you pass a Pydantic model class directly, automatically generating the underlying JSON schema from it, letting one single model definition drive both the schema constraint and the parsed result, exactly the unification benefit covered in that earlier topic.

code.content:
from pydantic import BaseModel

class Ticket(BaseModel):
    name: str
    priority: str

response = client.beta.chat.completions.parse(
    model="gpt-4", messages=messages, response_format=Ticket,
)
ticket = response.choices[0].message.parsed

blocks.text: 5. Best-Effort JSON Mode vs Strict Schema Mode

blocks.title: Diagram summary
blocks.content: Best effort JSON mode is compared against strict schema mode

blocks.text: A weaker option, requesting JSON mode without a specific schema, only guarantees syntactically valid JSON, not that it matches any particular structure, this connects directly to the reliability tiers covered in the earlier Schema-Based Outputs topic, strict schema mode is the meaningfully stronger option whenever a specific structure genuinely matters.

blocks.text: 6. Documented Limitations of Strict Mode

blocks.title: Diagram summary
blocks.content: Not every JSON schema feature is supported, check documented limitations first

blocks.text: Strict schema mode does not support every possible JSON schema feature, certain advanced schema constructs are documented as unsupported, checking the specific provider documentation before designing a schema avoids discovering an unsupported feature only after building against it.

blocks.title: This is a genuinely common gotcha worth checking upfront
blocks.content: A schema that works perfectly well as a general JSON schema definition can still hit an unsupported feature specifically in strict mode, checking documented limitations before finalizing a schema design saves real rework later.

blocks.text: 7. Structured Outputs With Function Calling

This connects directly to function calling, covered elsewhere in this module, and tool selection, covered in an earlier module, structured outputs and function calling solve related but distinct problems, structured outputs shapes the direct response content, function calling shapes how the model requests an external action, both can be used together in a genuinely agentic application.
8. A Worked Example

A support ticket classification feature defines a Pydantic model with name, priority as an enum, and resolved as a boolean, passes it directly through the SDK parse method, and receives back a fully typed, guaranteed-conforming Ticket object, ready to use directly in application code without additional parsing or validation for structure.
9. Still Worth Validating in Application Code

blocks.title: Diagram summary
blocks.content: Strict mode enabled is still worth validating in application code

blocks.text: This connects directly to output validation, covered in an earlier module, even with strict mode guaranteeing structural conformance, semantic validation, are the actual values reasonable for this specific business context, remains worth doing, structural correctness and semantic correctness are genuinely different concerns.
Worked Example

A team extracting structured data from support tickets initially uses plain JSON mode without a specific schema, occasionally receiving a response missing an expected field or using an unexpected field name, requiring extra defensive parsing code on their end.

Switching to strict schema mode with a Pydantic model passed directly through the SDK eliminates this inconsistency entirely, every response now reliably conforms to the exact expected structure, letting the team remove the defensive parsing code that strict mode conformance makes unnecessary.
Common Mistakes

items: Using plain JSON mode without a specific schema when a genuinely reliable structure is actually needed
Not checking documented strict mode limitations before finalizing a schema design
Manually maintaining a separate schema definition instead of passing a Pydantic model directly through the SDK
Assuming strict schema conformance eliminates the need for semantic validation of the actual field values

blocks.text: Practice

Define a Pydantic model for a structured extraction task you are familiar with, pass it directly through the SDK parse method with strict mode enabled, and confirm the returned object reliably conforms to your defined structure across several different test inputs.
Key Takeaway

OpenAI structured outputs, through the response_format parameter and strict schema mode, provides a concrete, strong implementation of the schema-based output reliability covered generally in an earlier module, especially powerful when combined with passing a Pydantic model directly through the SDK, though semantic validation of the actual values remains worthwhile even with structural conformance guaranteed.
